title: Choose the look for muzamilkhanrealtor.com (new set)
question: The roll picked 'Trail Map'. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Trail Map
options.lineage: East Bay Regional Parks trail maps (Tilden, Wildcat Canyon)
options.thesis: The East Bay as a trail map: flats to the hills in faint contour lines, each city a marked trailhead.
options.viewport: Your photo over a faint contour map of the hills, four city markers with their numbers, one 'Text me' action.
options.risk: Contours turn decorative fast; they must stay faint so your words and numbers lead.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by size alone: huge numbers, small labels, one typeface, no extra decoration.
Every city shows the same four numbers in the same order on every page, so they compare at a glance.

options.label: BART Map
options.lineage: BART system map and station signage
options.thesis: Your cities as stations on colored lines; every page is a stop you can see from the map.
options.viewport: A simple line map linking Berkeley, Oakland, Albany, El Cerrito, with your photo and one action.
options.risk: Transit-map design is a familiar trope.

options.label: Which City Fits You? Quiz
options.thesis: A short quiz that ends with the city that fits your budget and life.
options.viewport: Five quick questions, then 'Your city: Albany' with its playbook.
options.case: Fun and useful, but the magazine look undercuts trust for a $1M+ decision.
options.kept: A clear verdict at the end of a short path.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Giant type does all the work; nothing else on the page.
options.viewport: One huge number, '84%', and one line under it.
options.case: Bold and clean, but says little about you or the house.

options.label: Instrument Panel
options.thesis: Six calm gauges you cross-check at a glance.
options.viewport: Market gauges for each city on a dark panel.
options.case: Dark and technical, both things you moved away from.
options.kept: The same numbers in the same order, always.
options.risk: Feels like an app, not a person.

options.label: Cut-Paper Title Cards
options.thesis: One idea per full-screen color card.
options.viewport: A burnt-orange card with a cut-paper house.
options.case: Striking but artsy; buyers want facts fast.

options.label: Raku Ceramic
options.thesis: Soot-black and crackled silver, shaped by fire.
options.viewport: A dark crackled field with ember accents.
options.case: Beautiful but dark and unrelated to homes.

options.label: Gravity Garden
options.thesis: Rain that falls in every direction.
options.viewport: An animated garden with colored rain.
options.case: Pure art piece; no fit for buyers.
options.kept: Color as a guide to direction.

canonCard.label: The standard realtor site
canonCard.thesis: What top agent sites (Compass-style) ship, executed cleanly.
canonCard.viewport: Big photo of you, your cities as photo tiles, reviews, contact.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other agent site by design.
